messages:
amy.h: Quick check-in on Ivy-13B quant experiments — we ran int6 and int4 slices on the GTN traffic sample yesterday. Can someone paste the 1k-token unit econ + top-level quality deltas?
ben.k: Summary: int6 ~ 0.45 USD / 1k tokens, int4 ~ 0.28 USD / 1k tokens (batching & KV cache on). Latency median: int6 110ms, int4 95ms.
chris_r: Quality quick notes from the eval harness: overall ROUGE/EM-like metric drop vs fp16 is small (0.8 pts) for int6, larger for int4 (2.7 pts). But drops concentrated on long-context summarization and hallucination-sensitive slices.
elaine: Product impact: our GTN flows care a lot about factuality for receipts and billing summaries. On that slice int4 shows a ~4% regression in exact-match on key entities (date, total). Not catastrophic but noticeable in user QA.
amy.h: Can we get a compact scorecard (latency, cost, top-3 slice regressions) — we need to recommend routing defaults and a fallback plan. Also: is the int4 hallucination rate significantly higher on multi-step prompts?
miguel: Scorecard I ran (short): [FP16 / int6 / int4]
- cost /1k: 0.65 / 0.45 / 0.28
- p50 latency (ms): 95 / 110 / 95
- p95 latency (ms): 220 / 260 / 240
- key-entity EM (receipts): 0.92 / 0.91 / 0.88
- hallucination alerts (probe suite): baseline 1.0x / 1.05x / 1.28x
- recall on long-doc QA: baseline / -0.6% / -3.4%
(bench runs: 3k samples, mixed turns)
chris_r: Important: int4 shows higher variance on the long-tail prompts (rare tokens + long context), which explains p95 recovering a bit closer to int6. int4 often faster median but tail is noisy.
elaine: For GTN I'd propose: default route = int6, lower-priority prompts => int4. Add on-request override in the SDK: product can mark critical routes with `session.preference = "fp32|int6"` to force higher fidelity.
amy.h: That sounds reasonable. Any ops concerns for rolling int4 to a portion of traffic?
ops-bot: Canary rollout note: scheduled canary for Ivy-13B int4 on prod-sandbox at 5991116000. Auto-rollback on >1.5% error spike or >2.5% latency regression for 5m.
miguel: Also include a temporary quality gate: if hallucination-alerts >1.2x on canary we stop. I recommend starting at 5% of traffic and monitoring the `entity-exact-match` signal closely.
ben.k: One more econ note: with aggressive batching (batch size 32) int4 cost drops to ~0.22 /1k, but that increases p95 by ~15%. If product can tolerate slightly higher tail we can push more to int4 and save ~30% spend.
amy.h: TL;DR for GTN: Start with int6 default, 5% int4 canary (ops rules above), product flag to opt into int4 for low-risk flows, monitor `entity-exact-match` and `hallucination-alerts`, re-evaluate after 1 week.
elaine: I'll draft the recommendation for GTN and include the mini-scorecard. Will share the doc link after this thread. :+1:
miguel: Link to the raw bench run and probe suite: https://internal.redwood/infer/bench/ivy13b/599111 (internal)
amy.h: Great — thanks all. If anyone wants the raw CSV I can upload it to the shared drive.
chris_r: Upload would be helpful for anyone doing deeper slice analysis. I'll start a quick follow-up to examine hallucination triggers for int4 (tokenization edge cases maybe).
ops-bot: Canary started at 5991116000 (simulated) — monitoring hooks active.
elaine: Noted. I'll tag product and GTN owners in the doc.
